The Senate’s move to gut NFA taxes and registration for suppressors, SBRs, and SBSs is a surgical strike against bureaucratic tyranny. The Hearing Protection Act (H.R. 404) isn’t just about silencers—it’s about dismantling the IRS’s chokehold on constitutional rights. Forcing Americans to pay $200 and beg permission to exercise the Second Amendment is theft disguised as regulation.

The Fair Tax Act’s principles apply here: taxation shouldn’t be a weapon against liberty. Critics whining about the Byrd Rule miss the point—this isn’t policy tinkering. It’s exposing how the NFA’s 1934 framework was always a revenue racket, not a crime-fighting tool.

Washington’s addiction to taxing rights ends now.
